description: The SAME production patch as dcext824-derived-principal-neutralize (DCExtension.IsFileAttachmentPrincipal reverted to exact-type equality), checked instead against FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuardDerivedPrincipalTests824.SaveChanges_ForgedCrossTenantDerivedPrincipalFK_Tph_RejectedByGuard_NotPersisted, which drives a real SaveChanges call through FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard.BuildMap end to end (a forged Invoice.SignedFileId pointing at a different tenant's TPH-derived SignedFileTph824 row) rather than calling the predicate directly. Included specifically because, before this predicate was shared, BuildMap had an independent, unproven copy of this comparison -- a cross-vendor review reverted BuildMap's own line and found the whole assembly (5015 tests) had nothing that caught it. This entry is that missing signal: the same mutation the predicate-level test structurally cannot see (it never calls BuildMap) IS caught here because this test reaches the guard's actual code path directly. Note the sibling TPT guard-level test is NOT a valid green_test for this mutant -- it also depends on the derived-principal comparison and would go red too, since this mutation targets the SHARED helper both TPH and TPT consumers call. green_tests is instead FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuardBypassPathTests824's direct-DbSet-writer test, whose principal is FileAttachment itself (exact type, not derived) and therefore stays correctly protected under this exact-type-only mutation -- proving the mutation's blast radius is scoped to the derived-principal comparison and does not collaterally disable the guard's ordinary, non-derived case.
target_symbol: DCExtension.IsFileAttachmentPrincipal(Type?) -- the shared derived-principal IsAssignableFrom comparison, line ~250
